name: GHRP-3
lead: GHRP-3 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP), one of a numbered series of small peptides that act on the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor to stimulate growth hormone release.[1] Within physique and anti-ageing circles, growth hormone secretagogues are discussed as a way to raise the body's own growth hormone and IGF-1, with the hoped-for outcomes being more muscle, less fat and better recovery. GHRP-3 is listed by name among the peptides prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency.[2]

The published literature on GHRP-3 specifically is thin. It appears mainly in anti-doping analytical chemistry papers, and no completed human trial was found. A registered phase 1/2 study of continuous GHRP-3 infusion was withdrawn before enrolment.[4] Most community and clinical discussion concerns better-known members of the class, such as GHRP-6 and GHRP-2, rather than GHRP-3 itself.[1][5]

chain: Raises growth hormone release, with IGF-1 changes in the class
Claimed support for lean mass, fat loss and recovery
angle.text: Users of growth hormone-releasing peptides say that raising growth hormone helps them look leaner and fuller and recover from training. This is a claim made for the class and has not been tested for GHRP-3 in published human trials.

paras: GHRP-3 belongs to the numbered family of growth hormone-releasing peptides that Wikipedia lists as GHRP-1 through GHRP-6, alongside related secretagogues such as ipamorelin, examorelin and ghrelin itself [1]. These peptides are called synthetic ghrelin mimetics because they act on the receptor for ghrelin, the hormone that signals hunger and also stimulates growth hormone release [10]. The better-known member of the series, GHRP-6, is described as a synthetic analogue of met-enkephalin containing unnatural D-amino acids and having no opioid activity [10].

GHRP-3 has no dedicated encyclopedia article and is listed by name only [1]. Its appearance-related appeal is that of the class: raising the body's own growth hormone is discussed as a route to leaner, fuller-looking muscle and faster recovery between sessions, which in turn is meant to allow more training [1].

Growth hormone secretagogues act on the ghrelin/GH secretagogue receptor (GHSR) or the GHRH receptor, and many also raise IGF-1, prolactin and cortisol. Wikipedia's overview groups GHRP-2, GHRP-6, hexarelin, ipamorelin and ibutamoren (MK-677) as GHSR agonists and lists GHRP-3 in name lists without further description.[1] The main clinical use of the class is the diagnosis and treatment of growth hormone deficiency.[1]
GHRPs are small peptides of under 2 kDa, a size range that anti-doping laboratories screen together with related substances in urine.[2][3]

The class is divided by receptor. GHRH receptor agonists such as sermorelin and CJC-1295 act on one pathway, while ghrelin-receptor agonists, including the GHRPs, act on another, and the two mechanisms are described as distinct [1]. For GHRP-6, Wikipedia reports an oral bioavailability under 1% and an elimination half-life of about 2.5 hours in a study of nine healthy men, and notes that carbohydrate or fat intake around administration blunts the growth hormone response; these figures concern GHRP-6, and none have been published for GHRP-3 [10]. Ghrelin-receptor stimulation is also associated with increased appetite, which forum users of GHRP-6 describe [8][10].

Anti-doping laboratories have published methods for detecting GHRP-1 through GHRP-6 and related peptides in urine, and studies of in vitro metabolites of prohibited peptides have included this class.[2][3] The relevant papers describe GHRPs as small peptides that raise endogenous growth hormone and were developed with performance enhancement in mind.

Bodybuilding forums such as T Nation have hosted long threads on GHRP-6 and combinations with other peptides; GHRP-3 is rarely the peptide in those conversations.[5][6] Peptides of this type are sold online as research chemicals and are not approved as medicines for cosmetic or performance use.

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding settings, peptides of this class are generally discussed as part of larger stacks that may include anabolic steroids, IGF-1 variants and growth hormone itself, which makes the contribution of any single peptide hard to separate [5][6][9]. Wikipedia notes that GHRP-6 is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list [10], and anti-doping laboratories have published methods that screen for GHRP-3 together with related peptides [2][3].

No studies found. One registered phase 1/2 trial of continuous GHRP-3 infusion, examining the growth hormone-IGF-I system, blood pressure, glucose and insulin resistance, started in 2008 and was withdrawn before enrolment.[4] A 1997 University College London thesis catalogued physiological studies of growth hormone releasing peptides in man, covering the class.[7]

lore.intro: Community material in this class concentrates on GHRP-6 and GHRP-2; the posts below concern those relatives and are included because GHRP-3 belongs to the same family.[5][6][8]

claims.claim: GHRP peptides help users look leaner and fuller
claims.believers: A T Nation poster starting GHRP-6 says muscles felt fuller, that they seemed to have lost water weight and that they looked surprisingly leaner within days.[8]
claims.experts: The sources on GHRP-3 report no human results; growth hormone secretagogues in general have been studied mainly in growth hormone deficiency.[1][4]

claims.claim: Combining a GHRP with another releasing peptide gives a larger growth hormone pulse
claims.believers: Posters in a GHRP-6 advice thread describe pairing it with CJC-1295 and say the combination raises the pulse of growth hormone.[6]
claims.experts: Wikipedia classes CJC-1295 as a GHRH receptor agonist and GHRPs as GHSR agonists, two separate mechanisms.[1] No published trial of GHRP-3 in such a pairing is known.

claims.claim: Peptides are an alternative to injecting growth hormone itself
claims.believers: Users on T Nation compare peptide combinations with growth hormone for cost and effect.[9]
claims.experts: Anti-doping authorities prohibit the class in competition, and GHRP-3 is named in published detection methods.[2][3]

card.summary: A little-studied growth hormone-releasing peptide known mainly from anti-doping lists.
card.note: Prohibited in competitive sport; no completed human trials found.

quick.overview:
GHRP-3 is one of a numbered family of synthetic peptides that stimulate growth hormone release. It is discussed in muscle-building contexts as a growth hormone secretagogue.

Published work on it is mostly analytical chemistry for doping control. No completed human trial was found.
quick.mechanism: Like other GHRPs, it is classed as an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor.
quick.risks: No safety data from human trials were found. It is named on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list and is not an approved medicine.
